title: Appeals and Grievances Case Count per Beneficiary
content:
**Appeals and Grievances — number of cases per beneficiary (desk guide)**

A beneficiary may have any number of Appeals and Grievances cases. There is no limit on how many cases one beneficiary holds, at any tier or across tiers. The one limit that applies is per subject record: only one open case per subject record, under the one-open-case rule for Appeals and Grievances.

| Situation | Effect |
|---|---|
| A beneficiary already holds decided, dismissed or withdrawn cases and files a new one on a different subject | The number of cases held is no bar; no limit per beneficiary applies |
| A beneficiary holds an open case on one claim line and files on a different claim line | The number of cases held is no bar; each subject record is looked at separately |
| A beneficiary files a second case on the subject record of a case that is still open | Governed by the one-open-case rule, not by any count of cases per beneficiary |

**Basis Q&A**

*Is there a ceiling on cases per beneficiary?* No. The number of cases a beneficiary may have is unlimited; the only restriction is one open case per subject record.
